TITLE: Reasonable Limits: Proportionality Analysis Under Section 1
AUTHOR: A. Whitfield
SOURCE: (2023) 61 Osgoode Hall L.J. 112
YEAR: 2023

I. Introduction
The Oakes framework remains the dominant analytical tool for assessing whether a Charter infringement is a reasonable limit prescribed by law.1 Since its adoption, courts have refined the minimal impairment branch considerably.2

II. The Minimal Impairment Branch
Minimal impairment does not require the legislature to have chosen the least intrusive means available, only a means that falls within a range of reasonable alternatives.3 This deferential formulation has attracted sustained academic criticism.4

1. R. v. Oakes, [1986] 1 S.C.R. 103.
2. RJR-MacDonald Inc. v. Canada (Attorney General), [1995] 3 S.C.R. 199.
3. Alberta v. Hutterian Brethren of Wilson Colony, 2009 SCC 37.
4. See generally P. Hogg, Constitutional Law of Canada, 5th ed.
